findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:881 — OptimizedCursorPaginator passes negative offsets to Django QuerySet slicing, raising ValueError and causing HTTP 500 responses for advanced requests with negative cursors
src/sentry/api/paginator.py:839 — get_item_key() applies math.floor()/math.ceil() to a datetime ordering field, raising TypeError when building cursors for a non-empty optimized page

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — organization_context.member can be None for non-member callers using scoped authentication, so dereferencing .has_global_access can raise AttributeError when optimized_pagination=true

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The shared paginator does not clamp negative offsets for previous-page cursors, allowing negative is_prev cursors to cause ValueError during QuerySet slicing across BasePaginator subclasses

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The shared paginator does not clamp negative offsets for previous-page cursors, allowing negative is_prev cursors to cause ValueError during QuerySet slicing across BasePaginator subclasses

adjudication.rationale: The diff at line 182 shows that in BasePaginator.get_result(), the code now uses `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. This means when cursor.is_prev is True, the offset is used directly without clamping to 0. If a negative offset is passed with is_prev=True, this would result in negative slicing like `queryset[-5:stop]` which could cause unexpected behavior or ValueError in Django QuerySet slicing. The finding correctly identifies that negative offsets are not clamped for previous-page cursors in the shared BasePaginator code.
